units.sourceHTML: Classes
units.originalInnerHTML: Classes

units.sourceHTML: Every value in Wren is an object, and every object is an instance of a class. Even ⟦CODE0⟧ and ⟦CODE1⟧ are full-featured objects—instances of the Bool class.
units.originalInnerHTML: Every value in Wren is an object, and every object is an instance of a class. Even true and false are full-featured objects—instances of the Bool class.

units.sourceHTML: Classes define an objects behavior and state. Behavior is defined by methods which live in the class. Every object of the same class supports the same methods. State is defined in fields, whose values are stored in each instance.
units.originalInnerHTML: Classes define an objects behavior and state. Behavior is defined by methods which live in the class. Every object of the same class supports the same methods. State is defined in fields, whose values are stored in each instance.

The ⟦CODE0⟧ keyword says we’re defining a constructor, and ⟦CODE1⟧ is its
name. In Wren, all constructors have names. The word “new” isn’t special to

units.sourceHTML:
Note that we have to declare a constructor because, unlike some other
languages, Wren doesn’t give you a default one. This is useful because some
classes aren’t designed to be constructed. If you have an abstract base class
that just contains methods to be inherited by other classes, it doesn’t need
and won’t have a constructor.

units.sourceHTML: Like other methods, constructors can obviously have arguments, and can be overloaded by arity. A constructor must be a named method with a (possibly empty) argument list. Operators, getters, and setters cannot be constructors.

That rule applies to ⟦CODE2⟧ as well, return handles that implicitly inside
a constructor, so just ⟦CODE3⟧ is enough.

It is valid to use return inside of a constructor, but it is an error to have an expression after the return. That rule applies to return this as well, return handles that implicitly inside a constructor, so just return is enough.

units.sourceHTML: When a field name appears, Wren looks for the nearest enclosing class and looks up the field on the instance of that class. Field names cannot be used outside of an instance method. They can be used inside a function in a method. Wren will look outside any nested functions until it finds an enclosing method.

Field names cannot be used outside of an instance method. They can be used inside a function in a method. Wren will look outside any nested functions until it finds an enclosing method.
